blocks.text: Contraceptive counselling is a major O&G OSCE area. The master list includes counselling, combined oral contraception, progestogen-only contraception, implants, injectables, IUCDs, LNG-IUS, emergency contraception, postpartum contraception, adolescent contraception and contraception in women with medical conditions

The examiner is not simply testing whether you can **list contraceptives**. They want to see whether you can determine what matters to the patient, identify contraindications, explain options clearly, respect reproductive autonomy, and help the patient make an informed choice.

blocks.text: **LARC methods**, particularly implants and intrauterine methods, because their effectiveness is less dependent on user adherence.

blocks.text: **Copper IUCD**, as well as appropriate emergency contraceptive pills.

Q7. What is an important contraindication to combined hormonal contraception?

blocks.text: Previous VTE, migraine with aura, significant uncontrolled hypertension, certain cardiovascular disease, current breast cancer and other method-specific contraindications.

content_groups.group_title: Q8. What should you check before inserting an IUCD?

blocks.text: Pregnancy status, infection risk, unexplained bleeding and relevant uterine/cervical pathology, together with the specific eligibility criteria for the device.
